raw_analysis_notes: VBR+0x2A is the checksum-algorithm selector, but the value is only CONSULTED when volume-flag bit 0x40 (VBR+0x2C) is set: InitializeVcbFromBootSector initialises the type to 2 and overrides it from the boot sector only under that gate (refs_win11.decomp.c:487460 'bVar6 = 2;', :487473-475 'if ((*(uint *)(param_3 + 0x2c) & 0x40) != 0) { bVar6 = *(byte *)(param_3 + 0x2a); }', then VCB+0x31c = bVar6; the same three lines in insider at 531289-531293). The v3.4 driver never reads VBR+0x2a in that function at all. So '0 = None' does not describe a v3.4 volume: win10refsmini has VBR 0x2A = 0x00 and VBR 0x2C = 0x06 (bit 0x40 CLEAR) yet its metadata is fully checksummed - integrity --checksums verifies 17 of 17 page references as CRC64 with 0 mismatches and recomputes 13 of 13 root-table pages to their stored CRC64, and the CHKP self-descriptor is cktype 1 (CRC32-C) and verifies. Read the page-reference form (CHKP+0x5C) for what is actually in use, not VBR+0x2A alone.

description: Flags: 0x0080 = CRC32-C per cluster, 0x0100 = CRC64 per cluster: written (17134 CmsCrc64::InitChecksumBlobStream |= 0x100 :231412; 26100.9444 CmsStream::InsertRun sets 0x80 when the stream checksum type is 1, else 0x100, :17145-17151) and read (17134 SmsRunHeader::GetChecksumType: 0x180 clear = none, 0x80 = type 1, 0x100 = type 2, :113787-113790; 26100.9444 the 0x180 mask, :124610); no corpus extent row carries 0x100. Bit 0x0010 means WRITTEN, as of the row version that carries it (E113, N63): a run whose flags word is known and has 0x10 clear was allocated but not written when that row version was committed, and its clusters are not the file's content. Rows carrying 0x40 WITHOUT 0x10 number 267 of 571 on win10refs8g (v3.4), 214/512 on win10refs5g64k, 532/1,593 on win10refs2tspecials, 1,254/2,724 on win11refstestmftecmd and 976/162,098 on winsider -- their clusters can hold bytes, but those bytes are another file's or a later write's (winsider: 693 such runs serve foreign bytes, among them readable text). description: $DATA: the file's content stream. Whether its bytes are INLINE in the record or in on-disk EXTENTS is a property of the VOLUME FORMAT, not of the attribute: on format <=3.10 main $DATA is never inline (Prade et al.'s 'always non-resident' is correct, scoped to those formats); from format 3.11 it is inline while the stream is under 0x800 (2048 B). The 0x20000 (128 KiB) figure is the NAMED-STREAM cap, not a main-data threshold (see MD_ADS_RA_003), and named streams are NOT 'always resident' - 729 of 8,238 are extent-backed. Residency must be read from the $DATA descriptor's own form, never from the name row's length or its key_flags (E77/E87).

description: Hard-link support is gated by BOOT-SECTOR volume-flag bit 0x20 (VBR+0x2C), read once at mount - not by a checkpoint flag, and not confined to v3.14. Static: in all five v3.14-era builds InitializeVcbFromBootSector writes VCB+0x2acc = ((VBR+0x2c >> 5) & 1) | 0x38, and RefsHardlinksSupported is exactly 'return *(short*)(VCB+0x2acc) == 0x39'; RefsSetLinkInfo returns 0xC00000BB when it is false, and RefsCommonQueryVolumeInfo ORs 0x400400 into the FS attributes when true. No checkpoint field appears anywhere in that path. In win10 (v3.4) both the symbol and offset 0x2acc are absent from the entire decompilation and its own InitializeVcbFromBootSector never writes a hard-link field - genuine absence, established by reading the writer rather than by failing to find a name. Three volumes carry VBR bit 0x20 SET with CHKP+0x78 bit 0x080 CLEAR and all three hold hard links - win1121h2test (v3.7) 74 backings with >=2 back-pointers, win1122h2test (v3.9) 84, win1122h2test_afteropenedwithinsider 169.

description: CHKP root reference sizes: 0x68(3.4), 0x30(3.14/CRC64), 0x48(3.14/SHA256)
static_analysis_notes: ValidateCheckpointRecord derives NOTHING from the checksum type or version flags. Read in all six builds (win10 17134 CmsVolume::ValidateCheckpointRecord @1c00664c0, 511 bytes; the 3.14/insider builds carry the same body in the lambda at 26100.8115 @1401052ac, called from ValidateCheckpointRecordCallback @140105e10). It does five things: (1) ComputeOrVerifySelfChecksumBlock over the page, passing the self-descriptor words at page+0x58/+0x5C; (2) root count = u32@+0x90, required 4 < count <= page_size>>2; (3) per root, the OFFSET is read from the u32 array at +0x94+4*i and bounded (>= count*4+0x98, <= page_size, offset+0x28 <= page_size, 8-byte aligned); (4) each root's own length = u32 at root+0x24, bounded against page_size; (5) +0x88/+0x8C bounds. The only version-dependent behaviour is an indirection, not a size: when page+0x78 & 0x200 AND CmsVolume::VersionCheck(0x30b), the offsets array base is u32@+0x94 rather than 0x94 (SmsCheckpointRecord::GetGlobalTableOffset @1400b5fbc).
raw_analysis_notes: Reference size determined by version+checksum combination. 3.14 uses compacted references

description: Extent entry is 24 bytes: VLCN(4) + VLCN_hi(4) + flags(4) + file_VCN(4) + pad(4) + run_length(4) CORRECTION (E86 / MD_DATA_RA_024): the field at +0x08 is TWO u16s - flags at +0x08 and the RECORD SIZE at +0x0A - not a u32 flags word. Record size is 24 for a plain run and 24 + run*4 when flags bit 0x80 is set (per-cluster CRC32-C follows, 4 bytes each). Reading the pair as one u32 yields (record_size<<16)|flags, which is why every flag constant quoted here begins 0x18 (= 24, the plain record size). Records are laid out 8-BYTE ALIGNED, so the step to the next record is roundup8(record_size). Measured over 48,474 records / 40 images (0 violations) and 30,524 consecutive row pairs (99.6% gap == roundup8(record_size); the rest are unused node space).

description: Mount on a volume with a DAMAGED primary SUPB self-heals it, and the checkpoint activity below is that repair, not a clean-volume mount. The cited pair differs by exactly ONE 4 KiB block and ONE byte: image offset 0x101e055 = primary SUPB (LCN 0x1E) + 0x55, 0x2A -> 0xD5, inside the 16-byte Volume GUID at SUPB+0x50, which breaks that copy's self-checksum. Mounting then reverts that byte (0xD5 -> 0x2A) and the reopened SUPB cluster is byte-identical to the pristine one; the mount also writes 83 further 4 KiB blocks / 34,782 bytes and advances the CHKP virtual clock 64 -> 91. Do not cite these figures as the cost of a normal mount. The repair is DRIVER-DEPENDENT: byte 0x101e055 reads 0x2A before corruption and 0xD5 after, returns to 0x2A when the volume is opened with v3.14, and stays 0xD5 when it is opened with v3.4 - so the 3.4 driver did not heal it here -- although 17134's ReadSuperBlock has the same repair (17134 :53353-53390), its RefsMountVolume refuses a boot sector whose minor version is above 4 (0xC000014F, :265777-265778) before reaching it.

description: Integrity stream extents use variable-size rows. A checksummed row has flags 0xD0 and row size 24 + 4 x run (its declared size at +0x0A is the rule, flags bit 0x80 a cross-check; E99): the 24-byte extent, then one CRC-32C per cluster, the next row at the size rounded up to 8; runs from 1 to 223 are observed (record_size 916 with run 223). 0x1C00D0 is not a flag value but flags 0x00D0 | (row size 0x1C << 16), the run == 1 case, so a walk that tests the u32 for 0x1C00D0 misparses every checksummed row with run > 1 (E86, E99). Rows without a CRC slot have row size 24 (e.g. flags 0x180040). Table header format identical to normal extents. Re-stated 2026-11-12 (RUNNING_LOG N188): the row described checksum rows by the retired 0x1C00D0 test.

description: Deep allocator row structure: key=[range_start,range_length]. Two value forms, told apart by flags bit 0 (set = the row carries a bitmap): a bitmap row (bitmap offset u8 @0x14 = 0x18, a format byte u8 @0x15 (1 or 2: Container and Small 1 on every version, Medium 1 on v3.4 and 2 on v3.7+), a variable bitmap of ceil(range_length/8) bytes rounded up to 8, 1 = allocated; 2,072 bytes only for a 16,384-cluster range) and a compact row without bitmap (free u16 @0x10: 0 = fully allocated, non-zero = fully free). The free count @0x10 is authoritative (it saturates at 0xFFFF on compact rows); @0x16 is an allocated-cluster hint, not a usable used count (E74). Three-tier: Small (real LCN root #12), Medium (virtual root #1), Container (virtual root #2)

description: OID monotonic assignment: user OIDs start at 0x701: MsSetMinimumNewObjectId seeds the counter with 0x700 and GenerateIdentifier increments the counter atomically and returns its new value (26100.9444 :150897, :232562-232607; the four published samples' outputs hold 0 occurrences of 0x700 against 40-2,316 of 0x701; E155). An OID is not issued twice by the 26100 and Insider builds read: DeleteIdentifier never decrements the counter, the counter is stored in the Object Table root at checkpoint and reloaded at mount (FS_OTBL_RA_010); over the change journals of 42 corpus images (all 3.14) no directory OID is created again after its delete (0 of 13,907 deleted directory OIDs, counted per image). The 17134 driver does not store it: at each mount the counter restarts from the largest live OID, so after a remount a deleted directory whose OID was above every live one has its OID issued again (read in the driver, not measured: no 3.4 corpus volume has a change journal; E173). A gap is a deleted object or a failed creation: GenerateIdentifier commits the counter in its own top-level action, and OpenFileSystemFile, RefsAllocateObjectId's only caller, draws a directory OID before the directory exists (the failed-creation case is not measured); only directories draw user OIDs (E155). Confirmed on 66+ images and by static analysis across 3 driver versions (128 OID functions decompiled, see FS_OTBL_SA_001-010).

description: RefsIsBootSectorOurs: validates boot-sector ownership. Read in all six builds (insider 29574 @1402c5e54, 344 bytes; identical elsewhere but win10 uses VCB+0x198 for the sector-count bound). In order: two global disable flags == 0; device sector size (VCB+0x114) > 0xFF; bytes 3..10 == 'ReFS\0\0\0\0'; 0x57 < u16@+0x14 <= devsec; a ROR1+ADD self-checksum over bytes 3..u16@+0x14-1 skipping +0x16/+0x17, compared with u16@+0x16 - the strongest check in the function; bytes-per-sector at +0x20 in the RANGE 0x200..0x1000 (test: value - 0x200 < 0xe01), NOT a power-of-two test; sectors-per-cluster at +0x24 in the SET {1,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512} (mask 0x8000000080008089 on spc-1, plus 0x80/0x100/0x200), also not a power-of-two test; u64@+0x18 != 0 AND <= VCB+0x1f0; finally VCB+0x118/0x120 <= spc*devsec. Returns BOOLEAN. Both literals 0xe01 and 0x8000000080008089 occur 2/2 in every build.

description: key_flags is u16 at key+0x02, NOT the first 4 bytes of the row header. Values 0x68/0x2a8 are row sizes. key_flags take ONLY {0x01, 0x02}; 0x04 NEVER appears. description: $OBJ_LINK (type 0x39 on v3.7+, 0x38 on v3.4) stores a filename + parent OID inside the object's own record. There is ONE ROW PER NAME, not one per object (CORRECTED by E77 item 3, which falsified the earlier 'one-per-object; a hard link adds no new row'): the number of DISTINCT (parent OID, name) pairs equals the number of directory entries pointing at the object. It is the driver's own link list, so it is the authoritative answer to 'what are this object's names' and the basis for hard-link grouping. Two caveats when counting: some backings carry the SAME pair twice, byte-for-byte (deduplicate), and the rows exist only on objects with their own record - 0 of 219 embedded (key_flags 0x01) file rows carry one, and on v3.4 every directory carries one, the marker-less type-0x38 row (445 of 445 directories over the 13 v3.4 image paths, RC3_1.13.0/CORRECTIONS.md K114; the 0/309 was a scan that matched only the v3.7+ marker form, K114's reading; E77 as updated) (corrected 2026-11-21, RUNNING_LOG N639). Enables path reconstruction from the Object Table alone. Driver: RefsInitializeObjLinkRow.

description: MLog FOUR-layer model (resolves B2b): each data page = a LogCore data record. L1 = 0x78 (120)-byte record header (sig@0x00 + per-volume-magic@0x04 NOT-CRC + ver=1@0x08 + log-block-size-0x1000@0x0C + UUID@0x10 + counter@0x20 + LSN@0x28 + prevLSN@0x30 + length-in-4K-blocks@0x38/0x3C + entry-offset@0x54=0x78). L2 = entry header @record+0x78 (LSN@+0x00 + checksum@+0x08 + payload-len@+0x20 + payload-offset@+0x28 + type@+0x30=2-data/1-control). L3 = redo block _SmsRedoHeader @record+0xB0. L4 = _SmsRedoRecord entries. L4 NOTE (E97): the record's PAYLOAD holds a CHAIN of up to 15 merged redo blocks -- next block = first_off + total_size, and each block's record budget is its own total_size (CmsRestarter::ForEachBlockInMergedBlock / ForEachRedoInBlock).
static_analysis_notes: LogCoreWriteDataRecord + LogCoreScanDataRecord + LogValidateEntryHeader + LogInitializeEntryHeader; offsets identical in win10 (v3.4) win11 (v3.14) and insider. Entry payload-offset value is version-dependent: 0x38 (v3.4-v3.14) vs 0x40 (Insider; entry header 56->64B; redo block 0xB0->0xB8).

description: Primary and backup boot sectors can DIVERGE in the version field, and the driver cannot detect it. ReFS reads sector 0 (primary) at mount, and the backup only when that read fails with an I/O error (RefsReadBootSector win11 @135981 / ReadBootSectorForMount insider @231636; E122), at sector floor(P / 64 MiB) x (64 MiB / sector size) - 1 of the partition: `*(VCB+0x1f0)-1` while VCB+0x1F0 holds the partition length rounded down to 64 MiB (KNOWLEDGE_INTAKE A67 / A68; WAVEC_READING_bounds K3; corrected 2026-11-12: the row said both are read, the backup at totalSectors-1). Validation `RefsIsBootSectorOurs` (win11 @483985) is self-contained — signature + the ROR1+ADD u16 self-checksum at 0x16 (exactly `forefst._vbr_checksum`, now confirmed against the driver) + geometry sanity (0x18/0x20/0x24). There is NO cross-copy CRC64 and NO virtual clock, so the two copies' relative currency is undecidable; the backup is consulted only when the primary read physically FAILS (the fallback loop breaks on read success regardless of validity). Forensic consequences (RD): (a) on a genuine upgrade the backup retains the ORIGINAL pre-upgrade version — confirmed on TWO independent real upgrades: win10to11refs4g_afterwin11mount (primary v3.14 / backup v3.4) and win1122h2test_afteropenedwithinsider (v3.14 / v3.9); only bytes 0x29 (minor) + 0x17 (checksum) differ. This recovers the EXACT original version (vs $VolInfo's "pre-v3.10"). (b) The same divergence reveals VBR tampering: on hand-edited test images the primary carries the altered version (6.66, 3.15) while the backup holds the authentic 3.14. Static caveat (mechanism undetermined): the in-driver RW-mount upgrade dual-writes both copies (RefsWriteBootSector @135517, gated only by the SMR flag CmsVol+0xd34&0x800000), so both *should* be rewritten — yet the backup keeps the old version on every observed upgrade. The offline-tool hypothesis is ruled out: refsutil has no version-upgrade command (applets are dedup/snapshot/salvage/rollback/compression/triage/fixleaks/fixboot/iometrics), and its sole VBR writer `CFixBoot::Execute` (@140032770) also dual-writes primary + backup (decompiled). So the divergence seems to originate inside the driver's own upgrade path — the backup write apparently skipped on the upgrade transaction, or the version stamped via a sector-0-only path — but the exact reason is not pinned down. The empirical signal (backup retains the original version on 2 independent upgrades) is solid; the mechanism is not. Surfaced by `integrity` (Redundancy section reports the version mismatch + both versions, honestly "upgrade or tampering"). | Why the measured upgrades kept the old backup (N654, 2026-11-21): the upgrade write reaches sector 0 only (FS_VBR_RA_014), and both volumes already carried flag 0x02, so the later write that would carry the version to the backup did not fire.

description: Deleted directory entries are recoverable in B+-tree NODE SLACK — and no current tool method gets them. Both tools' B+-tree iterators drive strictly off the live row-offset array `[thoff+astart, thoff+aend)`; the ~13 KB of slack in a 16 KB page is never read. Deletion (`CmsBPlusTable::DeleteFromIndex` @14001a610) removes the offset-array slot, marks the row (+0x08 bit 0x4, `MarkIndexEntryDeleted`; E181) and queues *delayed* compaction — row bytes are not scrubbed; they persist until a later CoW rewrite. Validated 0 false positives on the clean baseline (all 19 recovered names genuinely absent from the live tree); robust v3.4/64K/corrupt. description: Per-name MACB divergence across hard-link names -- a journal-independent timestomp cross-check. Each hard-link name is an independent type-0x30 non-resident row with its own copy of the file's four times, Created(value+0x10)/Modified(+0x18)/Changed(+0x20)/Accessed(+0x28) (NTFS hard links share one $SI; each NTFS link has its own $FILE_NAME times). A name-scoped SetFileTime writes the file's OWN RECORD at once, for every name; what diverges is each NAME'S INDEX ENTRY, a lazily refreshed cache refreshed only for the name a handle was opened through: when that handle sets the basic information, the allocation or the end of file (RefsUpdateFileDupInfo, whose only callers are RefsSetBasicInfo, RefsSetAllocationInfo and RefsSetEndOfFileInfo) and on its close path (RefsCommonCleanup -> RefsUpdateDuplicateInfo) (E112 as amended 2026-11-12; 26100.8115 and .9444). So an un-opened sibling still holds its pre-stomp Created (LAB-L: an open, a 1-byte read and a close through the name refreshed it, two directory listings did not -- which of the three steps did it is not shown, E143). Divergence is evidence; agreement clears nothing (a read of the sibling produces it too); the stale entry is the name nobody OPENED, not the name nobody FORGED, so WHICH name holds the authentic birth is NOT established. The signal is perishable: an open of the file through the stale sibling erases it (a listing alone does not, E143). See E59; supersedes the '#335 one-timestamp-set / no cross-check' framing for hard-linked files. Re-stated 2026-11-12 (RUNNING_LOG N179): the row called it ReFS-only and 'stronger than NTFS $SI-vs-$FN (NTFS hard links share one $SI and cannot diverge)'.

description: The FileId ordinal at $SI+0x58 (= the low 8 bytes of the 128-bit Windows file id) is the OBJECT'S OWN ordinal, not a 'next' counter: on lab314_main the embedded type-0x30 value+0x80 equals Windows' FileIdLo from fsutil on 4,645 of 4,645 rows matched by (FileIdHi == containing-dir OID, name), 0 disagreements, and all 27 ground-truth directories read FileIdLo 0 (a directory's own type-0x10 value+0x80 is 0 on 26 of 26 that have such a row). description: Allocator row format (E74), correcting four points of structure_reference B.2. (1) The bitmap row is VARIABLE length: bitmap_offset + roundup8(ceil(range_length/8)); 2072 B is only the range_length=16384 case (also 152 for 1024 clusters, 32 for 12 and 3). (2) +0x14 is TWO u8 fields, not a u16 'header size': bitmap_offset u8@0x14 (0x18 with a bitmap, 0x00 without) and a format byte u8@0x15 that is TIER-dependent - Container and Small are 1 on every version, Medium is 1 on v3.4 and 2 on v3.7+. (3) Flags BIT 0 means 'this row carries a bitmap' - the discriminator the driver uses; values 0x01/0x05/0x09 (bitmap) and 0x02/0x06 (compact) are consequences. (4) +0x16 is NOT a usable used-count: it is a driver-maintained allocated hint with 0xFFFF meaning 'the entire range', it disagrees with the row's own bitmap on 742 of 4634 rows, and must never be used for capacity arithmetic. +0x10 (free) IS authoritative but SATURATES at 0xFFFF (it does not truncate) - impossible on a bitmap row (range <= 16384), so it affects compact rows only. ROW ADDRESSES ARE PHYSICAL cluster numbers for the Medium tier (NOT stated by B.2, and a different question from B.2's Addressing column which describes how each tier's TABLE PAGES are reached): the Medium span is exactly [0, last-mapped-physical-cluster) on every image while the virtual space starts at first_container_id<<shift and is ~2x wider; live file-data extents are marked allocated 99-100% by translated PLCN vs 0-27% by VLCN. Container/Small row address basis NOT established. Authoritative free count: bitmap row = range_length - popcount(bitmap); compact row = 0 if free_u16==0 else range_length. Compact-row discriminator is free_u16 (0 = fully allocated, non-zero = fully free, and then free_u16 == min(range_length,0xFFFF)); this REFUTES the earlier working guess that the discriminator was +0x16.

description: ReFS 3.4 ADS are stored with a MARKER-LESS embedded 0xB0 key (E75): the attribute type sits at key+0x08 and the UTF-16 stream name starts at key+0x0C, whereas from v3.7 an instance marker (0x80000002/0x80000001) occupies key+0x08, the type moves to key+0x0C and the name to key+0x10 - the two-form rule E72/MD_LK_RA_006 already recorded for embedded keys in general. A 0xB0 reader that matches only the marker form therefore reports ZERO alternate data streams on every v3.4 volume. Both forms must be accepted and the name read at the offset the matched form implies. The ADS-vs-snapshot discriminator is unchanged (StreamSummary val+0x10: 0=ADS, 2=snapshot, E61). Marker-less 0xB0 rows also survive on volumes UPGRADED from v3.4 (retained pre-marker entries), so the rule is not purely version-gated and must be applied per-record. These rows are typically NOT at the outer level of the embedded tree - they are reached only via the E73 index-node descent, which is why an outer-level census reported none.
static_analysis_notes: Key layout is the E72/MD_LK_RA_006 two-form rule (marker era boundary v3.4<->v3.7, corroborated by unsound/refsprogs' explicit version>=3.5 branch). The 0xB0 attribute type and the StreamSummary ADS/snapshot discriminator at val+0x10 are the documented E61/C11 fields.

description: Authoritative file size for a non-resident object (E76). A type-0x30 index-entry name (key_flags 0x02) caches the file size at value+0x38; the OBJECT's size is the type-0x40 backing's value+0x58. The cache is not refreshed on every update and can be stale in BOTH directions - larger than the object (an over-read that appends cluster slack) or SMALLER (a silent truncation, the dangerous case). Any size that gates a read or a write must resolve through the backing when one exists and fall back to the name's field only when it does not. Structurally impossible on v3.4, which has no type-0x40 rows and no key_flags 0x02 FILE rows (only kf=2 directories), so the rule keys on 'a backing resolves' rather than on the volume version.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation. The rule rests on the on-disk corroboration below: the backing's +0x58 agrees with the independently-decoded $DATA stream size where the name's cache does not. The type-0x40 backing layout itself is the documented C.3a structure.

description: Every MLog LogCore record carries its own 8-byte integrity value at entry_header+0x08 (= page+0x80 where the entry header offset at page+0x54 is 0x78), and the algorithm is REPRODUCIBLE (E78). It is a four-way interleaved u64 XOR folded to 32 bits, not a CRC: zero the 8-byte field itself, then for each log block of le32(page,0x0C) bytes (0x1000 on every volume, independent of the cluster size) accumulate acc[i mod 4] ^= each little-endian u64, XOR the four accumulators together, and fold the result 64->32 as (v>>32) ^ (v & 0xFFFFFFFF). Blocks chain: the next block's acc[0] is seeded with rotate-left-1 of the previous block's result. A record is exactly one block, so in practice the seed is 0. The field is present on BOTH record types at entry_header+0x30: type 1 (control page) and type 2 (data record); no other type exists on disk. The per-volume constant at page+0x04 is a format/log-instance magic, NOT a checksum - reading it as a per-record checksum finds the same value on every record. Because it is an XOR fold it is an integrity check, not a signature: it detects any single altered bit, but with a seed of 0 the result is the XOR of all the block's 32-bit words, so it is blind to ANY reordering of those words and to any set of changes whose XOR cancels (E78 as amended 2026-11-12, N182).
static_analysis_notes: Written by LogCoreWriteDataRecord and verified by LogVerifyChecksumEntryHeader -> LogChecksumBlock on recovery; the log block size is hard-set to 0x1000 by MlLogOpenLog (record+0x0C).

description: The $UsnJrnl:$J journal is an IN-PLACE RING, not an NTFS-style front-trimmed sparse file (E79). A record whose USN is X sits at byte offset X modulo the stream's ALLOCATION, the extents start at file VCN 0, and old records are overwritten where they lie. Consequence for a reader: the whole allocation must be read and the buffer may hold TWO generations at once - the newest records are at the START of the buffer and the oldest in the middle, so byte order is not time order and the highest USN legitimately exceeds the stream's size. Under the alternative (front-trimming) the live extents would begin past VCN 0 and offsets would be USN minus a base; that is refuted below.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation; the on-disk observation below is decisive on its own because it is a controlled discriminator between the two candidate models. | 26100.9444 RefsFileOffsetFromUsn :182390-182398: offset = USN - VCB+0x3C8 (the USN at file offset 0), or (VCB+0x3D0 - base) + USN below the base, 0 beyond VCB+0x3D8: a record sits at its USN within the ring (the base a multiple of the ring length on the disk, E170).
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02. 14 corpus journals, 338,439 of 338,439 records satisfy USN mod allocation == byte offset. The decisive case is winsider.raw, the only journal that has WRAPPED: allocation 33,554,432 B (32 MiB, extents (VCN 0, 6021 cl) + (VCN 6021, 2171 cl) = 8,192 clusters exactly), highest USN 74,459,840 = 2.22 windows, and ALL 217,892 records have USN >= the allocation, so the modulo is never the trivial identity. The buffer holds exactly two generations: generation 1 occupies offsets 7,352,320..33,554,168 and generation 2 occupies 0..7,350,976 - a clean partition with the write head at ~7.35 MB, which is the signature of a ring that has wrapped once. 0 violations. Non-circular: parse_usn_records derives `offset` from the linear scan position and reads `usn` from the record body, so the two quantities are independent. This settles the experiment the reference itself specified for the question.

description: The size of a type-0x30 index-entry value (key_flags 0x02) is fixed AT WRITE TIME by the driver version that created the entry - 72 bytes (0x48) below v3.10, 84 bytes (0x54) from v3.10 - and is NEVER rewritten afterwards (E80). It is therefore NOT a property of the volume: a volume UPGRADED across that boundary carries BOTH layouts side by side, its pre-upgrade entries keeping the 72-byte form while the newer driver writes 84-byte entries for anything new. A reader must take the entry size from the row's own length, never from the volume version; keying on the version misparses every retained entry on an upgraded volume. All fields the tools read live at or below value+0x44, which is identical in both layouts, so a length RANGE test (0x48 <= len <= 84) is correct and version-independent.
static_analysis_notes: The write-time gate is explicit in RefsAddFileNameIndexEntry: the value length is 0x48 when the version is below 0x309 and 0x54 otherwise. The driver applies it when ADDING an entry, which is why existing entries survive an upgrade unchanged.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02, whole 99-image corpus: 2,172 x 72-byte and 113,356 x 84-byte index-entry values. Exactly 3 images carry BOTH, and all 3 are the corpus's UPGRADED volumes (forefst summary: APPEARS UPGRADED): win10to11refs4g and win10to11refs4g_afterwin11mount (32 x 72 B + 6 x 84 B) and win1122h2test_afteropenedwithinsider (482 x 72 B + 333 x 84 B). Every NATIVE volume carries one size only, matching its format-time version. Two controlled BEFORE/AFTER pairs prove the retention on two independent upgrade paths: win10to11refs4g_beforewin11mount (v3.4, 33 x 72 B, 0 x 84 B) -> win10to11refs4g (v3.14, 32 x 72 B + 6 x 84 B), and win1122h2test (v3.9, 482 x 72 B, 0 x 84 B) -> win1122h2test_afteropenedwithinsider (v3.14, the SAME 482 x 72 B retained + 333 x 84 B new). No tool change: forefst already tests the length range rather than the version.

description: The REPARSE_DATA_BUFFER of a DIRECTORY reparse point (junction or directory symlink) is NOT a top-level type-0xC0 row in the object's table: it lives INSIDE the object record's embedded attribute tree (E81). The object's table holds a single row keyed 0x10 whose value carries the embedded tree - typically 0xC0 (reparse), 0x90 and 0x39 - and the parent's name row is an 84-byte index entry with no room for a buffer. The embedded 0xC0 value has a 12-byte header whose u32 at +0x08 is the offset of the standard REPARSE_DATA_BUFFER (tag u32@0x00, ReparseDataLength u16@0x04, Reserved u16@0x06, then SubstituteNameOffset/Length and PrintNameOffset/Length u16 pairs; path buffer at +0x14 for SYMLINK, which carries a 4-byte Flags field, and +0x10 for MOUNT_POINT). A reader that scans only top-level rows reports these targets as absent although they are fully present on disk. A junction commonly carries PrintNameLength 0, so the SubstituteName is the authoritative fallback and the target must never degrade to the tag NAME. Same wrong-level class as E73 (attributes in a child node), so the embedded parse must be given the descent context or an object with a large attribute set is missed a second way.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation. The buffer itself is the documented Windows REPARSE_DATA_BUFFER; what is established here is WHERE ReFS stores it for a directory reparse point, which the on-disk evidence below settles.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02, whole 99-image corpus: of 341 reparse-bearing objects, 243 carry 0xC0 at the top level and 98 carry it ONLY embedded - including 78 of 81 on the real Windows volume winsider.raw. Decoding the embedded buffers yields real targets (\??\C:\ProgramData, \??\C:\Users\Default, Program Files, Common Files, Internet Explorer, Windows Defender, Microsoft Shared - the Windows compatibility junctions). NON-CIRCULAR ground truth: the lab generator writes its own CSV log onto the volume; extracting forefst_test2_log_20260705_085450.csv from win11refs8g gives the 8 reparse points it created with their intended targets. Before the fix the tool found all 8 and resolved the 6 FILE symlink targets byte-for-byte but reported NO target for the 2 DIRECTORY ones (junction1, sym_dir_abs); after it, both resolve to the generator's recorded R:\forefst_test2\reparse\rp_target_dir (the junction via its NT-namespace SubstituteName \??\R:\...). Corpus effect of the fix: 98 targets GAINED over 11 images, 0 changed, 0 lost - strictly additive.

description: Record PLACEMENT and data RESIDENCY are independent axes (E82). A key_flags 0x02 name means the object's record was split out into a type-0x40 backing - what a move or a hard link forces - and says NOTHING about where the file's bytes live. The bytes can remain INSIDE that backing: its MAIN $DATA sub-record (single-instance marker 0x80000001 + type 0x80) is then the RESIDENT form - summary_size@0x0C=0x30, storage_type@0x10=0, byte count at +0x20, content at +0x3C. The alternative is the extent-bearing stream record (inner_hdr@0x00=0x88, summary_size 0x200 on v3.14+ / 0x1A0 on v3.4-v3.10, extents at +0x88); the two forms are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. Two reader traps: an ADS is a MULTI-instance (0x80000002) 0x80 row, so matching any 0x80 row returns a stream that is not the file's data; and the backing must be joined on the PAIR (stream_idx = name value+0x00, home = name value+0x08) -> backing key (+0x08, +0x10), because stream indices are unique per home, not globally. Consequence: a reader that infers residency from key_flags reports these files non-resident and cannot recover their content, though it is in the record already held.
static_analysis_notes: The driver's read path validates the attribute with RefsCheckValidResidentDataAttribute and reads the bytes IN PLACE at content offset 0x38 from the attribute header (= value+0x3C); it never consults a name-row placement flag, so residency is a property of the ATTRIBUTE. RefsAllocateNonResidentDataAttribute is the separate path that moves a stream out.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02, whole 99-image corpus: 16,191 of 83,176 key_flags 0x02 files keep their data inline in the backing, over 26 images (winsider 14,580 of 72,709); mutually exclusive with the extent-bearing form (0 records carry both). Content validated on 400+ sampled files: 400/400 inline length == stated size == the name's cached size; 56/57 .xml parse as well-formed XML; 13/13 .png carry the PNG magic; 5/5 .json parse. NON-CIRCULAR ground truth: the lab generator wrote hl1_/hl2_/hl3_ hard links as exactly 400 bytes of a repeated marker (New-Marked "HL1BODY_" 400, corroborated by its own on-volume STATE log size=400) and the recovered bytes are BYTE-EXACT 7/7. Extends C.3a, which already recorded the phenomenon at backing+0x60 (alloc == size for small files stored resident inside the backing, 6,794/6,823 sub-cluster backings on winsider) but gave no decode for the content. Tool effect: extract/dataruns/export previously failed 'no extents decoded' on these and now read them (25/25 sampled across 3 images, 0 content mismatches); IsResident corrected on 14,118 cells over 14 images, with no other CSV column and no row count changed.

description: Stream snapshots are copy-on-write, so a snapshotted file's data is SHARED across its streams (E83). A block is duplicated only when it is about to be OVERWRITTEN; every block unmodified since a snapshot stays shared - present once on disk, listed in the snapshot's extent table and ABSENT from the current stream's. Consequence for the $DATA stream record: disk_alloc@0x48 is what THIS stream owns (what its own extent list covers) while total_alloc@0x30 is the FILE's whole allocation, so they diverge exactly by the shared (or sparse) blocks. Reading any version means resolving each file VCN across the streams: for the CURRENT stream a missing VCN comes from the NEWEST snapshot holding it (a block only leaves the current table while unchanged); for a PRIOR version only snapshots STRICTLY OLDER may be used, since a newer snapshot can hold content written after the version being recovered. A VCN no stream holds is a genuine sparse hole. A reader that assembles a stream from its own extents alone returns the full size with the shared blocks ZERO-FILLED - bytes present nowhere on the volume.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation; the on-disk evidence is decisive on its own because the stream record's own extent-count field confirms the short extent list, and the reconstruction is validated byte-exact against independently recorded generator content.

description: A non-inline stream's EXTENT record (the type-0x0 sub-record of E61) is identified by its key SHAPE: key_offset 0x10, key_size 0x50, and attribute type 0x0003 at key+0x08 (E84 - confirms the refsprogs-sourced MD_ADS_RP_001 and sharpens it). Every such record carries a plausible stream size at value+0x38, which is the link back to the 0xB0 stream descriptor. The key itself carries NO stream name - the name is in the 0xB0 descriptor - so 'named-stream extent key' describes the record's purpose, not its key content. A reader must NOT identify the record by a zero byte at key[12]: a DIFFERENT record (14-byte key, attribute type 0x0080 at key+0x08) also satisfies that, and value+0x38 is not a stream size there.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation; the discriminator is established by the exhaustive on-disk split below (key shape vs plausibility of the stream-size field), which separates the two record types with no overlap.

Neither key form contains a decodable UTF-16 name. description: An extent entry's cluster number in an inline 0x10028 holder is a VIRTUAL LCN and must be validated by TRANSLATION, never by comparison against the volume's physical cluster count (E85). The virtual address space is wider than the physical one - it begins at (first_container_id << shift) and runs roughly twice as far (E74) - so a plausibility test of the form 0 < vlcn < physical_cluster_count rejects every extent that lives in the upper half of the virtual space. Because a greedy decoder stops at the first entry it cannot validate, one rejected entry makes the whole extent map decode as EMPTY and the file appears to have an undecodable/overflow holder. The correct test is whether the container table can map the VLCN; a physical bound is only a fallback where no translator is available. A sparse hole (flags & 0x20; its VLCN mirrors its file VCN, so vlcn == 0 catches only a hole at file VCN 0: E98, E146) is valid and zero-filled, never read.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation; the on-disk proof is decisive - the rejected VLCN translates cleanly through the documented container table and the clusters it names reproduce the volume's own recorded SHA-256.

description: A file's extent map is a B+-tree NODE inside its $DATA record, not a flat run array (E86). The current stream's $DATA value carries at value+0x88 a node with the standard 0x28-byte header: level at +0x0C (0 = leaf, non-zero = index), row count at +0x14, the key-index array's start and end at +0x10 / +0x20 ((+0x20 - +0x10) / 4 = +0x14), the end of the rows at +0x04, and the index array of 4-byte slots (u16 row offset, u16 word that is not reliably the file VCN: the row's own +0x0C is) (E151). LEAF rows are the standard 24-byte C.4 extent entries (VLCN +0x00, file VCN +0x0C, run +0x14). INDEX rows carry the standard 48-byte four-LCN node reference; those LCNs are VIRTUAL and the child page holds the same node at 0x50 + u32@page+0x50, so the walk is uniform and recursive. NEW FIELD: record_size at +0x0A is 24 for a plain run and 24 + run*4 when the stream carries per-cluster CRC32-C (flag bit 0x80 at +0x08), the trailing u32s being those checksums, 4 bytes each. The field takes 136 distinct values (24..1048) and for checksummed records tracks the run across the full observed range (run 11->68, 66->288, 100->424, 122->512, 223->916), which a high-half-of-flags reading cannot produce. Records are 8-BYTE ALIGNED: the step to the next record is roundup8(record_size), measured on 30,524 consecutive row pairs (30,405 match; 428 genuinely padded; 119 larger gaps = unused node space, harmless because rows are addressed by the index array). This also explains WHICH files failed before: the old walk advanced '32 if u32@+0x08 == 0x1c00d0 else 24', and 0x1c00d0 is only the run==1 case, so a checksummed record with run>1 (u32 0x020000d0 at run 122) made it advance 24 and land mid-record - 19 of the 21 unreadable files on the reference volume were integrity streams. This CORRECTS C.4/C.4a: entry+0x08 is u16 flags + u16 row_size, not a u32 flags field - reading the pair as one u32 gives (row_size<<16)|flags, which is why every documented flag constant begins 0x18 (= 24, the plain row size). The $DATA row MUST be selected on the sub-stream id at key+0x10 == 0x1000: a file with snapshots carries one $DATA row per version (0x1001, 0x1002, ...) under the same key prefix, so choosing by value size or first match returns a SNAPSHOT's extents and presents that older version's bytes as the live file. Resolves the residual recorded in C.3b.
static_analysis_notes: Decoded from the on-disk bytes; the node header, level byte and 48-byte four-LCN child reference are the same shapes the driver's own B+-tree walk uses elsewhere (already E2-confirmed for page-level nodes).
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-03. Row-size rule measured over 48,474 extent rows across 40 images: 0 violations of row_size == 24 + (flags&0x80 ? run*4 : 0); observed flag lows 0x40/0x50/0x60 (plain, row_size 24, 47,728 rows) and 0xD0 (checksummed, 746 rows). NON-CIRCULAR ground truth: win11bidule ships the operator's own SHA-256 inventory written on Windows before the image reached this project - files matching it go from 608 to 629 of 629, 0 mismatch. The 21 gained were all >1 MB (19 integrity-stream drivers, a 782 MB archive, a 791 MB ISO) and each had previously failed CLEANLY with 0 bytes; verified end-to-end through extract, including the 791 MB file. Structure present on 54 of 100 corpus images. The sub-stream selector is not cosmetic: selecting the $DATA row by size returned tests/secret.txt's 79-byte pre-truncation snapshot text as the live 25-byte file - caught by hash comparison, not assumption. Implemented as a FALLBACK ONLY (runs where the existing cascade yielded nothing), with _contiguous_cover still applied, so an incomplete walk yields no extents rather than wrong bytes and no previously-resolving file can change. Two decoder defects surfaced while validating this: tr.tr() does NOT raise on a container-table miss - it falls back to IDENTITY (VLCN read as PLCN) and counts the miss, so a direct call would accept an unmappable row and read the WRONG clusters (now tested as (vlcn >> tr.shift) in tr.map, without the counter); and because that counter is surfaced to the analyst as 'N VLCN(s) had no container mapping - output may be incomplete', probing rows that never become extents moved it (541->550 on one image with nothing incomplete). Translation is now deferred until a cover is accepted. With both fixed the whole-corpus output fingerprint (3,496 runs) shows dataruns byte-identical to the previous release on every image. Breadth of the gain, measured on the whole-corpus fingerprint: dataruns reports 48 MORE files with decoded extents across 7 images (winsider 58,127->58,144; win1122h2test x3 +7 each; win1121h2test 174->178; win11bidule 3->8; win11refs8gcompresszstddefault 103->104), 0 files lost and no existing extent list altered. Only win11bidule carries an operator SHA-256 inventory, so the other images' gains are corroborated rather than proven: all 48 gained files extract to REAL content (0 empty, 0 all-zero, 0 near-constant - the shapes a wrong physical address produces), and win1121h2test testintegrity/xbpt_tango_archive_828215.dat opens with the lab generator's own GFSAREPLAY marker. description: Data residency is decided by a VOLUME-FORMAT gate, not by size alone. RefsAddAllocationForResidentWrite branches on the volume format version read from the VCB (CONCAT11(vcb[0x318],vcb[0x319]) vs 0x30b=3.11): on format <3.11 a inline write >0x20000 (128 KiB) raises 0xC0000427 STATUS_FILE_SYSTEM_LIMITATION (the v3.4 path calls RefsTelemetryUnsupportedADS, identifying it as the named-stream cap) and an already-inline stream NEVER converts; on format >=3.11 the stream stays inline only while size < 0x800 (2048 B), else RefsConvertToNonResident. Main $DATA is never created resident before format 3.11, so <=3.10 volumes are always extent-backed. Snapshot creation, block-clone, encryption, remote/tiering and strictly-sequential each convert an inline stream to extents regardless of size; an explicit set-allocation / set-EOF converts only when the new size is 2 KiB or more (26100.8115 RefsSetAllocationInfo :494981-:494990, RefsSetEndOfFileInfo :495307-:495311); integrity does not convert a stream, it makes the file extent-backed at birth (E107). (Corrected 2026-11-21, RUNNING_LOG N638.) The gate reads the VOLUME's format, so an upgrade affects future writes only and converts nothing retroactively.
static_analysis_notes: RefsAddAllocationForResidentWrite win11 26100 @1400ddd2c: version gate CONCAT11(vcb[0x318],vcb[0x319]) < 0x30b; error branch 0x20000 -> RefsRaiseStatusInternal(-0x3ffffbd9 = 0xC0000427), WPP trace logs 0xc0000427; residency branch 'format<0x30b || size<0x800' stays resident else RefsConvertToNonResident. win10 17134 @1c00b05a0 has NO conversion branch and calls RefsTelemetryUnsupportedADS on the >0x20000 path; RefsConvertToNonResident is ABSENT from the v3.4 driver (0 refs; 15 each in win11 26100 / 26100.8521 / Insider 29574). RefsCheckValidResidentDataAttribute exists only in the v3.14-era drivers. Complete v3.14 caller set of RefsConvertToNonResident: CreateStreamSnapshot, DuplicateExtents, AddAllocationForResidentWrite, ReplaceDataAttribute, SetEncryption, CascadesSetFileRemote, SetFileStrictlySequential, SetAllocationInfo, SetEndOfFileInfo.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-04, 523,756 rows / 117 openable paths = 79 distinct volumes (507,433 rows) (ab_census.py, path-keyed and completeness-asserted; verified by ab_verify_census.py). Format <=3.10: 7,006 rows / 18 images (v3.4,3.7,3.9,3.10) INLINE=0 and EMPTY=0, every row extent-backed, smallest 5 B holding a full 4 KiB cluster. Format >=3.11: largest inline 2,047 B, 0 of 408,670 inline rows reach 2,048 (= the driver's 0x800); that ceiling is measured on 4 KiB-cluster volumes (408,656 rows) - 64 KiB volumes contribute only 14 inline rows (max 1,685), too few to establish a ceiling there. description: READER DEFECT found 2026-09-04, FIXED in v1.10 (E89) -- this row said 'NOT fixed' through v1.10.0-v1.11.0 and is corrected 2026-09-08. A key_flags 0x02 name whose HOME object is never walked as a directory had no type-0x40 backing in walk_directory_tree's t40_content map (keyed (owner_oid, stream_idx), filled only from directories the walk visits), so resolution fell to the solo branch with rec=None and data_inline was left unset; files then reported IsResident=False although the backing's $DATA was the inline form. Content was never affected: extract resolves the backing on demand via _home_streams and returned the right bytes, labelled resident/inline. Fix applied in v1.10: the walk gained the same cached on-demand obj_map[home] lookup (_home_t40). The pre-fix join stayed reachable behind --legacy-link-join in v1.10-v1.11.0; v1.11.1 removed the flag and the old ladder, so the home lookup is the only path. Re-measured 2026-09-08 by A/B against that flag over 124 in-scope images / 568,638 files: 1,012 rows differ, every one from data_form unset to the real form -- winsider 548 to inline (reproducing E89's 548 exactly) plus 456 to extents, and 8 to extents on win11refs2tmillionsofactionsv2; SecurityId changed on all 1,012, confirming the stated blast radius. description: Named streams follow the same 0x800 (2048 B) threshold as main $DATA on format >=3.11, one-directionally: NO named stream of 2048 B or more is inline, and extent-backed ones start at exactly 2048. Below 2 KiB a stream is inline UNLESS the writer pre-allocated (alloc != size; E60), which is why 13 sub-2KiB streams are extent-backed. The documented ATTRIBUTE-FLAGS u16 at value+0x02 is the exact discriminator: bit 0x1000 set <=> content is not inline (729 extent-backed + 115 snapshot-name), clear <=> inline or empty (7,509), 0 violations. 0xB0 rows with storage_type 2 are NOT an ADS storage form: they are named SNAPSHOT entries whose value+0x44 matches an existing $DATA sub-id > 0x1000 (115/115). The 0x20000 (128 KiB) cap is an error branch that fires only on format <3.11; on v3.14 a 131,072-byte named stream stores normally.
static_analysis_notes: RefsAddAllocationForResidentWrite win11 26100 @1400ddd2c: the 0x20000 raise is guarded by format <0x30b; the 0x800 branch is version-gated the same way for any inline stream. win10 17134 @1c00b05a0 reaches the 0x20000 raise via RefsTelemetryUnsupportedADS, naming the limit a NAMED-STREAM limit.

INLINE 7,505 (max 1,920 B), EMPTY 4, EXTENT 729 (716 of them >=2048 with min exactly 2048; 13 below 2048, ALL with alloc != size: adstest 30 B/alloc 4096 and 12 SmartScreen 7 B/alloc 4096). 0 inline rows >= 2048. Attribute-flags bit 0x1000 at value+0x02 partitions inline vs non-inline with 0 violations. description: The NAMED_DATA attribute-flags u16 at 0xB0 value+0x02 carries the named-stream residency discriminator. Bit 0x1000 is SET on every stream whose content is not inline (extent-backed streams and snapshot entries) and CLEAR on every inline stream and inline-form empty. This CORRECTS NAMED_DATA.md's parenthetical that 0x1000 'does not mean non-resident - such ADS are still inline': that reading is explained by 13 rows which look inline only if the E60 packed-allocation rule is not applied (an inline named stream stores its bytes packed, alloc == size; all 13 have alloc 4096 with size 7 or 30 and are extent-backed). Other bits observed but NOT interpreted: 0x0C00 accompanies 0x1000 on snapshot entries (giving 0x1C00, consistent with the page's existing HasSnapshot 0x0400 note), and 0x4000 accompanies 0x1000 on the 12 SmartScreen streams (giving 0x5000). Both recorded as observed, meaning not established - they are not named as flags.
static_analysis_notes: No driver citation for this field yet: the residency GATE is decompiled (RefsAddAllocationForResidentWrite, MD_DATA_RA_025) but the write of this flag is not traced. SECOND ELEMENT NOT AVAILABLE IN-WORKSPACE: refsprogs source is not present (only the 2026-08-29 audit ledger, which records refsprogs deciding residency 'by attribute form' at L9-I01 but does not quote this field), so the requested independent reading could not be checked. Corroboration used instead: the E60 packed-allocation rule, which is forefst's own validated extraction path, and the internal cross-check that every 0x1C00 row is a snapshot entry independently witnessed by a matching $DATA sub-id > 0x1000 (115/115).

Bit 0x1000 set on exactly 844 rows (729 extent-backed + 115 snapshot entries) and clear on exactly 7,509 (7,505 inline + 4 inline-form empty). ZERO violations of 'bit set <=> content not inline'. Observed values: 0x0000 (7,509), 0x1000 (717), 0x1C00 (115), 0x5000 (12).

description: The driver reads the VOLUME FORMAT VERSION from the VCB as two bytes at +0x318 (major) and +0x319 (minor), combined as CONCAT11(vcb[0x318], vcb[0x319]) - i.e. (major << 8) | minor, so format 3.11 is 0x30B. This is the field every format-gated behaviour branches on, and it is the VOLUME's format, not the driver's build: an up-to-date driver mounting an older-format volume takes the older branch. Observed comparison constants in v3.14: 0x30b (3.11) and 0x309 (3.9).
static_analysis_notes: refs.sys win11 26100: RefsAddAllocationForResidentWrite @1400ddd2c reads it twice, via the SCB's VCB pointer at scb+0x90. Six occurrences of the '< 0x30b' comparison and two of '< 0x309' in that build. The values compared are real ReFS FORMAT versions (3.9, 3.11), which a driver-version field would not be.
raw_analysis_notes: Behavioural confirmation on disk, without a VM: on win10to11refs4g (a v3.4 volume upgraded to v3.14) 0 of 262 pre-existing files changed residency, while the only inline file (desktop.ini, 129 B) is one of exactly 3 names that appear only AFTER the upgrade. Residency is therefore fixed at write time by the volume's then-current format, which is what a VCB-inline format field predicts.

description: $EFS DDF entry layout decoded. val[0x60] u32 = DDF entry count (1 on every observed record - single user, no data-recovery agent, so no DRF). The single DDF entry starts at val[0x64] with a 5-u32 header: [0x64] entry_len, [0x68] hash_len = 0x14 (SHA-1), [0x6C] wrapped-FEK length = 0x100 (RSA-2048), [0x70] FEK offset RELATIVE TO 0x64, [0x74] zero. Fixed-offset fields inside the entry: credential SID at val[0x94] (28B, S-1-5-21-...), public-key-info header at val[0xB0] (5 u32s, first = 0x14 hash length), certificate SHA-1 thumbprint at val[0xC4] (20B = 0xB0 + 0x14), container-GUID/CSP/key-container UTF-16LE strings from val[0xD8]. Two invariants hold on every record: 0x64 + entry_len == value_len - 2 and 0x64 + FEK_offset + 0x100 == value_len - 2, so the wrapped FEK is the entry's last field and the value carries 2 trailing bytes. Resolves both value sizes: FEK at val[0x1A2] on 676B records and val[0x1DA] on 732B.
static_analysis_notes: Not traced in the driver: EFS metadata is produced by the EFS service/cng.sys, not by refs.sys (GN_EFS_SA_001 records the driver-side integration only). The layout is the DPAPI/EFS DDF format, decoded here on disk.
raw_analysis_notes: 7/7 $EFS records over 3 images (win11refs4gattributestest2 4, win11refs4gattributes 2, wininsiderrefs2t 1) satisfy all four invariants: DDF count == 1, hash_len 0x14 / FEK 0x100 / pad 0 / pk[0] 0x14, 0x64+entry_len == len-2, 0x64+FEKoff+0x100 == len-2. Both value sizes present (676B x6, 732B x1). Thumbprint at 0xC4 is constant within a certificate set and differs between them, as a per-user cert must. BREADTH CAVEAT: v3.14+ only, DDF count 1 only - no multi-user or DRA-bearing record exists in the corpus, so the count>1 and DRF-present layouts are UNVERIFIED.

description: The page-reference checksum is computed over the WHOLE referenced PAGE - the concatenation of the cluster bytes of every valid LCN slot at page-reference +0x00..+0x18, read AFTER container translation - and is compared against the value at page-reference +0x28 (length from +0x24, algorithm from +0x22). In an Object-Table row the page reference begins at value+0x20, so the LCN slots are value+0x20..0x38 and the checksum is at value+0x48. Slot count is determined by cluster size, not by version: 4 slots on 4 KiB clusters and 1 on 64 KiB, both yielding one page (16 KiB / 64 KiB). Nothing is excluded from the digest - not the page header, not the page's own self-checksum field. Where an Object Table holds several rows for one object id, only the row the reader keeps (the last) is meaningful.
static_analysis_notes: Reproduced from the bytes rather than from the driver; the pre-v3.14 verification behaviour documented on the page (CmsChecksumNone stub) is a separate, decompilation-only claim and is untouched by this row.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-05, every Object-Table page reference on 89 images: 34,311 checked, 0 skipped. The invariant is scoped to the row the READER uses: an Object Table may carry MORE THAN ONE row per object id (an earlier generation and a current one) and build_object_map keeps the LAST. On that row the digest verifies 33,883/33,883 - 89/89 images, no carve-out, no tolerance. The remaining 428 references are SUPERSEDED rows; 408 of them still verify and 20 do not, which says nothing about the volume because nothing reads them. Duplicate rows occur on 4 images only (the win11refs2tmillionsofactions family, 107 of 200 oids doubled). By cluster size: 4 slots on every 4 KiB reference, 1 on every 64 KiB one, both making one page. Both algorithms exercised: type 0x02 CRC64 and type 0x04 SHA-256. | Y (2026-11-21, N669; analysis/reports/v1.13.2/RC1D/rc3a/y/ym1_ref_checksums.py, .json): every page reference read on the 124 corpus.lst volumes carries a checksum (type byte +0x22 / +0x42 not 0, length 8 or 32): the 1,612 root references of the chosen checkpoints (1,404 of 0x30 bytes, 156 of 0x68, 52 of 0x48), 98,702 inner-row references the table walks follow (97,998 CRC64, 704 SHA-256) and 89,008 Object Table rows; none without one.

description: PRE_FORMAT and CHANGE_LATE are NOT independent timestomp signals - they are the two halves of ONE event, and tiering their co-occurrence as corroboration is wrong. CORRECTED 2026-09-06: the pair does NOT establish that the event was a copy. Deliberately BACKDATING a creation time produces the identical pair (create/modify set to a pre-format value, change time at the moment of the write), so the signature is AMBIGUOUS between a timestamp-preserving copy and a backdate. Witness: a lab volume whose generator log records 74 SetCreationTimeUtc actions carries exactly this signature. The INFO tier therefore means 'ambiguous - corroborate with USN', NEVER 'not suspicion': the USN journal is the only independent source that separates the two causes. A copy that preserves timestamps (robocopy /COPY:T, restore, archive extraction) writes the ORIGINAL create/modify, which predate the volume (PRE_FORMAT), and sets the change time to the copy moment, which post-dates create/modify (CHANGE_LATE). The signature a copy CANNOT produce is CHANGE_LATE WITHOUT PRE_FORMAT - created on this volume and altered afterwards; it occurs on 384 files of one real Windows volume and is the MEDIUM tier's witness set.
static_analysis_notes: Mechanism is in the signal definitions themselves (timestomp_intrinsic_flags): CHANGE_LATE = change > max(create, modify) + margin; PRE_FORMAT = create < volume_create - margin. The tool's own docstring already noted CHANGE_LATE 'trips on a creation-time-preserving copy (robocopy /COPY:T, restore)'.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-06, base rates over the FULL corpus: 96 openable images / 521,060 files. Share of ALL files: PRE_FORMAT 118,126 = 22.67%; CHANGE_LATE 116,320 = 22.32%; CREATE_GT_MODIFY 5,410 = 1.04%; HARDLINK_MACB_MISMATCH 193 = 0.04%; ROUND_TIMESTAMPS 190 = 0.04%; FUTURE 4 = 0.00%. 23.6% of ALL files carry at least one intrinsic signal. Co-occurrence: CHANGE_LATE with PRE_FORMAT 115,936; CHANGE_LATE WITHOUT PRE_FORMAT 384 (0.33% of CHANGE_LATE), ALL on winsider.raw - a real Windows volume, the files being system components (Microsoft.UI.Xaml.winmd, DWriteCore.dll and similar) whose change time post-dates create/modify, consistent with servicing/installer metadata writes rather than tampering. So the pair is one copy signature 99.67% of the time, and the residual IS the MEDIUM cohort - created on this volume and altered afterwards, which a copy cannot produce. CONSEQUENCE: pre-1.10.1 tiering marked 22% of an ordinary volume MEDIUM-or-higher for having been copied onto it; since 1.10.1 a copy signature alone is INFO and HIGH is reserved for HARDLINK_MACB_MISMATCH (0.04%) and journal corroboration. Corpus-wide tier split after the change: HIGH 193 / MEDIUM 388 / INFO 122,348 of 122,929 flagged. PROVENANCE: an earlier draft of this row cited a 27-image subset (17.94%/12.43%/1.40%/0.31%) and stated 0 witnesses for CHANGE_LATE-without-PRE_FORMAT; that subset was lab-generated volumes only and the figure was wrong at corpus scale. PROVENANCE SPLIT (RD 2026-09-06, structural discriminator >1000 files under Windows/, NOT an xbpt_ filename heuristic which misclassifies winsider): the corpus is 1 REAL Windows install (winsider.raw, 120,617 files) + 95 LAB-built volumes (400,443 files). Flagged share: real 115,488 = 95.75% of files (HIGH 1, MEDIUM 384, LOW 0, INFO 115,103); lab 7,441 = 1.86% (HIGH 192, MEDIUM 4, LOW 0, INFO 7,245). The corpus AVERAGE of 22% therefore understates a real installed system by 4x - under the pre-1.10.1 tiering 95.4% of a real Windows volume was MEDIUM, i.e. the column flagged the operating system. Post-change the actionable set on that volume is 385 files. CAVEAT: the real-install cohort is n=1; treat the lab figures as a floor and the real figure as a single witness. UNCORROBORATED (2026-09-06): the 384 CHANGE_LATE-without-PRE_FORMAT files are the MEDIUM tier's entire witness set and they are INTRINSIC-only - no journal, hard-link or lab corroboration exists for any of them. Their reading as servicing/installer metadata writes is an INFERENCE from file identity (Microsoft.UI.Xaml.winmd, DWriteCore.dll and similar), not a measurement. They stay MEDIUM (look, not tampered) pending the T15 lab set, which must produce a known-good witness: a file created on the volume and then genuinely altered, versus one touched only by servicing, with the operator's own log as ground truth. Until then the tier rests on one volume and on reasoning, not on a controlled case. LABEL CORRECTION (2026-09-06): an earlier wording of this row and of the tool's own output called the pair a 'timestamp-preserving copy signature' and INFO 'reported, not suspicion'. That asserts a CAUSE the bytes cannot establish - a backdated creation is observationally identical - and it was contradicted by an operator generator log recording 74 SetCreationTimeUtc actions on a volume carrying the signature. The tier (INFO) is unchanged and still correct; only the claimed cause was wrong. | v1.11.0: the TimestompFlags column and the --timestomp flag were REMOVED from `files`. description: A sparse raw image cannot distinguish a genuinely zero-filled file from a region the acquisition never captured: both read as zeros. A hole in the image file is therefore NOT evidence of missing data - a file's own zero-runs are legitimately stored as holes. The only informative case is content that is ENTIRELY zero whose WHOLE allocation lies in holes, and even that is ambiguous. Tested with SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE on the image file, which is three-valued: a byte count, or undeterminable - never a silent 0.
static_analysis_notes: Not a driver behaviour: this is a property of the acquisition container, not of ReFS.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-06 over 96 images / 105,889 extent-backed files. All-zero content: 18. Of those, whole allocation in image holes: 15 (0.014% of files checked); undeterminable: 0; all-zero but NOT fully holed: 3 (correctly silent). The 15 are dominated by LEGITIMATELY zero-filled files - Windows DumpStack.log.tmp, several .TMContainer*.regtrans-ms transaction containers (512 KiB and 5 MiB), and 1 MiB lab .bin files - plus the one genuine case that prompted this: xbpt_victor_tango_152379.bin on win11refs2t64ksha256checksums (505,381 bytes, a well-formed 8-cluster map, every cluster in a hole). REFUTED EN ROUTE: an earlier version warned on ANY extent overlapping a hole; measured, a 791 MB ISO, a 1-second silent WAV and 245 files with correct GFSAREPLAY content all overlap holes and all extract CORRECTLY, so overlap alone is meaningless. The tool therefore reports and never suppresses bytes: zeros may be the file's real content.

description: OPERATION TABLE (E87 two axes). Record placement and data residency are independent, and each operation moves at most one of them. MEASURED: create small -> embedded x inline (format >=3.11); grow past the inline ceiling -> residency inline->extents, placement unchanged; truncate to 0 -> residency STAYS extents (one-way: every 26100 / Insider driver has RefsConvertToNonResident and none a ConvertToResident; 17134 has neither, so on it no conversion exists: corrected 2026-11-21, RUNNING_LOG N638); MOVE to another directory -> placement embedded->split, residency UNCHANGED; ADD A HARD LINK -> placement embedded->split, residency UNCHANGED; rename in place -> neither changes; snapshot then read -> residency extents->snapshot-shared; write to a snapshot-shared stream -> back to extents. The two bold cases are the point: a move or a hard link relocates the RECORD and moves NO DATA.

description: Timestomp tiering has no discrimination on a controlled set, and the command's printed legend contradicts its own tier function. T15 built 8 files with one known cause each. Six are flagged, ALL at INFO -- 0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM / 0 LOW over 603 flagged files. A file with all three timestamps backdated (3 signals: CHANGE_LATE|PRE_FORMAT|ROUND_TIMESTAMPS) is INFO because that set is a subset of _TS_COPY_SIGNATURE, which is correct -- a timestamp-preserving copy produces the same set -- but the legend printed above the table says 'HIGH = >=2 independent signals or 1 authoritative; MEDIUM = 1 strong intrinsic; LOW = a weak/single hint', which timestomp_verdict() never implements: HIGH comes only from an authoritative source (USN or hard-link), never from a signal count. HARD LINKS: the two type-0x30 name rows of the T15 pair are byte-identical on disk over their whole 84-byte value, timestamp block +0x10..+0x2F included, and the home backing record carries the same times -- because both names were opened after the call (the lab's Record-Truth step), and an open, a read and a close through a name refresh that name's entry; a SetFileTime refreshes only the name it was made through (E112, E143). The tool prints the per-name index-entry field (value+0x10/+0x18/+0x20/+0x28), never the backing's, so the identical output is faithful to the disk and not a resolution artefact -- the per-name hard-link MACB cross-check has nothing to detect because the names genuinely agree.

description: Deletion recovery is correctly keyed to DATA residency, not record placement -- but a remnant whose declared inline region reads as zeros was still reported as 'FULL FILE recoverable ... EXACT' and yielded a zero-filled file. Those zeros have TWO explanations -- the file held zeros, or the deletion took the bytes -- and nothing in the remnant separates them, so the outcome names both rather than asserting either. T17 deleted one file per class. Correct: del_inline (500 B inline) -> full content; del_split (500 B, MOVED then deleted, so a split record whose data stayed inline) -> full content, which is the E87 two-axes rule holding through deletion; del_extent and del_snap -> metadata only; recycle_me -> metadata + carve. DEFECT: the residency verdict is taken from the remnant's value LENGTH, not from whether the value actually carries the bytes. del_split's slack row carries a 1,336-byte value with only 104 non-zero bytes and no data pattern, so `export deleted` wrote 500 zero bytes and the manifest labelled them confidence=high, recoverable_inline, EXACT.
static_analysis_notes: forefst.py deleted/export-deleted: the recoverable_inline verdict keys on value_len, with no check that the value's data region is populated.

description: The MLog is a timestomp corroboration source where the change journal is not. Each call that sets a file's times is its own redo 0x04 (RedoUpdateDataWithRoot) on the file's table, carrying the whole $SI after the call; when the program leaves the change time to the driver (SetFileTime, the .NET setters) that field is the moment of the call (E171). SCOPE: the creating record corroborates the BIRTH time only; the time-setting records show any time that was set, and when. A record exists only while the log has not overwritten it. description: A stream snapshot does NOT keep a copy of the file's $SI timestamps. The 116-byte snapshot descriptor carries exactly one FILETIME, at descriptor+0x4C, and it is the moment the SNAPSHOT was taken (the system time) unless the stream's attribute flags carry 0x400, when it is copied from the existing snapshot descriptor (26100.9444 RefsCreateStreamSnapshot :161214-161220; which streams carry 0x400 was not traced) -- never a copy of a $SI field. Its position relative to the live $SI therefore reconstructs the operation order, and it is an independent witness against a stomped $SI: a creation time ABOVE the snapshot timestamp is impossible and therefore a contradiction between two structures. The reverse is not: a file must exist before it can be snapshotted, so C < snapshot ts is the NORMAL ordering and backdating only moves C further below it. Measured on lab314_main_step3, 3 of 3 snapshotted files show C < snapshot ts - including the deliberately backdated p07_snapshot_then_backdate.bin (C = 2023-09-12 17:02:57, snapshot 2026-09-12 17:03:17) and the row's own two untouched witnesses t12_cow.bin and t12_inline_kept.bin. The test catches FORWARD-dating, not backdating.

description: A boot-sector version LOWER than the volume's true format is SILENTLY REWRITTEN UPWARD AT MOUNT, and the self-checksum recomputed, so downward VBR version tampering ERASES ITSELF. RefsUpgradeVersionInBootSector (called from RefsMountVolume) compares boot+0x28/+0x29 against _VCB::GetVolumeUpgradeVersion and overwrites the pair only when the stored version is STRICTLY LESS (major < target, or major == target and minor < target); it then recomputes the ROR1+ADD self-checksum at +0x16 and calls RefsWriteBootSector, restoring both on write failure. Measured on the win11refsmini version-edit series, with the limits of that evidence stated: NO image in the corpus reads 3.12 (141 ReFS volumes scan as 3.4 x13, 3.7 x1, 3.9 x2, 3.10 x2, 3.14 x120, 3.15 x1, 6.66 x2), and all three VBR copies of both '...rechangedtoversion312' images read 3.14 / sha8 6759cfa5. The corpus holds only the POST-mount capture, so the bytes cannot distinguish 'edited to 3.12 then rewritten' from 'never edited' - the 3.12 step rests on the image's file name and the operator's account, not on a pre-mount witness. (The two images that were never mounted, 6.66_opened and 3.15, differ from the base in exactly one region, the boot sector, by 4 and 2 bytes.) An implausible version (6.66) is NOT rewritten and does not mount: the image is byte-identical before and after the open attempt and the checkpoint clock does not move (vclock 64). A version ABOVE the driver's own maximum was never mount-tested, so its behaviour is unmeasured. FORENSIC CONSEQUENCE: a VBR version consistent with the volume's structures does NOT prove the field was never altered -- one mount launders a downward edit, and the only trace is ordinary metadata churn. This QUALIFIES FS_VBR_RA_013: primary/backup divergence exposes UPWARD or invalid tampering (6.66, 3.15 survive untouched against an authentic 3.14 backup), but not a downward edit that has since been mounted. BACKUP COPY (resolved 2026-09-13): RefsWriteBootSector writes the backup LBA and then LBA 0, so a mount-time correction normally rewrites BOTH copies and leaves no primary/backup divergence for an examiner to find -- the erasure is complete, not partial. A device-object condition can reduce it to the primary alone. The format-UPGRADE path also reaches RefsWriteBootSector (K142, this row's static notes; RefsUpgradeVersionInBootSector clears the upgrade request at the next writable mount, master §A.1 bit 7, E5's amendment), so a missing call does not explain why the two measured upgrades kept the pre-upgrade version in the backup (FS_VBR_RA_013): that is not settled (corrected 2026-11-21, RUNNING_LOG N639). | Which copies the rewrite reaches (N654, 2026-11-21): RefsUpgradeVersionInBootSector runs before MsInitializeVolume creates the volume object (26100.9444 :426717 vs :426795), and RefsWriteBootSector writes the backup only when that object exists (VCB+0x70, :134344-134346), so the upgrade write reaches sector 0 only; the backup gets the new version only if the mount's later flag write fires (boot +0x2C bit 0x2 clear, :427077-427097).
static_analysis_notes: win11latest_c02d29ed (26100.8521): RefsUpgradeVersionInBootSector @14028fedc, sole caller RefsMountVolume; strict-less-than guard on boot+0x28/+0x29 vs _VCB::GetVolumeUpgradeVersion, then a checksum recompute and a write. CORRECTION (K142): the format-UPGRADE path DOES reach RefsWriteBootSector, so the claim that it does not is refuted. RefsWriteBootSector @14009afb0 has exactly two call sites - inside RefsUpgradeVersionInBootSector (L428474) and inside RefsReadWriteBootSector (L485818); the same 2+1 grep pattern holds in 8115, 8972 and 9444. RefsReadWriteBootSector @1402e6ddc is a 48-byte dispatcher: mode '\x03' reads, anything else writes. RefsMarkVolumeForUpgrade @140256a10 reads with mode 3, sets boot+0x2c |= 0x80 when bit 7 is clear, recomputes the ROR1+ADD checksum into +0x16, and writes with mode 4 - and mode 4 is a WRITE. So an upgrade does rewrite the boot sector; whatever leaves the pre-upgrade version in the backup copy, it is not the absence of this call.
raw_analysis_notes: RD. analysis/rawdisk/disks/step4continuing/win11refsmini_* version-edit series. A full 512-byte-aligned signature scan finds exactly THREE 'ReFS\0\0\0\0' copies per image: 0x1000000 (primary, at the partition start), 0x3110000, and 0x7cfffe00. The DRIVER's backup is the third, not the second: RefsWriteBootSector sets the target LBA to VCB+0x1f0 - 1, and InitializeVcbFromBootSector @1402e80ec assigns VCB+0x1f0 from the boot sector's TotalSectors at +0x18; here TotalSectors = 0x3e0000 with 512-byte sectors, so the backup LBA is 0x3dffff = image offset 0x1000000 + 0x3dffff*512 = 0x7cfffe00. The copy at 0x3110000 is partition-relative LCN 0x2110 and sits in the BitLocker (FVE) metadata reservation - 'FVE-EOW' at 0x3122000 and 'OLRDHEVF' at 0x3124000 follow it. The OBSERVATION is unaffected: both candidate copies read 3.14, sha8 6759cfa5, on all 15 images including the 6.66, 3.15 and 3.12-named edits.

description: Object Table value+0x18 is a 64-bit LOG SEQUENCE NUMBER, not a generation counter: u32[6] (value+0x18) = offset within a log segment, u32[7] (value+0x1C) = segment number. It records the log position at which that object was last modified, in the same address space as the checkpoint LSN at CHKP+0x70. Supersedes the 'generation counter = checkpoint virtual clock' reading (E104).
static_analysis_notes: The writer was not decompiled; the reading rests on a controlled disk experiment with a null control plus exact agreement with the checkpoint LSN, not on driver code.
raw_analysis_notes: LAB-G, 3 images of ONE volume: labG_0 creates dirA/dirB/dirC (f0..f4 each); labG_1 modifies one file in dirA ONLY; labG_2 modifies one file in dirB ONLY; dirC is never touched after creation (null control). dirA 0xa000008dd -> 0xb000008f1 -> unchanged; dirB unchanged -> unchanged -> 0xc00000906; dirC frozen on all three. 6/6 transitions as predicted, control never moved. CORROBORATION 15/15 volumes: max(u64 at value+0x18) == the active checkpoint's own LSN at CHKP+0x70 EXACTLY on the 3 LAB-G images and 12 randomly sampled corpus volumes (4K and 64K clusters, v3.4-v3.14, 2 GB to 2 TB, incl. one 4Kn) -- expected when the object table is written last at checkpoint time. REFUTES 'u32[6] = checkpoint virtual clock': the field takes 8-50 distinct values per volume (a clock has one) and on labG_0 the clock is 4020 while the field ranges 0..19907. Forensic use: orders object modifications in LOG time, independent of $SI timestamps an attacker can set, and identifies objects modified after a given checkpoint. No tool surfaces it yet.

description: CLEAN-DISMOUNT INVARIANT: on a cleanly dismounted volume the checkpoint is the last structure written, so max(Object-Table value+0x18 LSN) == CHKP+0x70 exactly. description: How a USN record is written: RefsWriteUsnJournalChanges -> RefsWriteFcbUsnRecordToJournal -> RefsUsnAppendData copies the record into a 4 KiB cache page of $J (CcPreparePinWrite with Zero=1 at a page start, otherwise CcPinRead) and dirties it with CcSetDirtyPinnedData(bcb, 0), with no LSN. The record bytes never reach the log (MLog): only the file's 16-byte $SI+0x40 pointer (LastUsn + journal id) is logged, as redo opcode 4, and only for a close record that is not a delete (FCB flag bit 0 clear). A record never straddles a 4 KiB page (the page tail is zero-filled). The record's time is taken from KUSER_SHARED_DATA when it is copied.
static_analysis_notes: Two blind readings (A10DOC_STATIC_READING_1.md, _2.md) compared in A10DOC_STATIC_COMPARISON.md: CONFIRMED WITH SCOPE on every build, no disagreement. Out of scope on every build: the cache manager's later write-back of the dirty page, references held only in data tables, whether $J can be resident, the disassembly (decompiled text only). 'Of $J' rests on the REFS_CHANGE_JOURNAL_FILE_NAME symbol and field use. On 8115/8521/8972/9444 the 4 unnamed AddRedoRecord callers were not traced; RefsCommonWrite's resident branch was read on 9549 only. Neither gap touches the record's own data flow (N389).

description: A file can point past the last record of the USN journal: its $SI LastUsn pointer is logged and replayed (MD_USN_SA_001), while the record itself is only in a dirty cache page of $J. On a volume captured before the page was written, page copies already carry pointers above the last surviving record; after a reboot the log replay brings the records' pointers into the tree. A LastUsn above the journal's last record is therefore not by itself evidence of tampering.
static_analysis_notes: Mechanism: MD_USN_SA_001 (E2, 7 builds).

description: A copy ends with its source's change time, older than the destination's own creation: a plain copy (Copy-Item, .NET File.Copy) carries the source's Modified and change time, robocopy /MOV all four of its times; in the MLog the destination's $SI record (redo 0x04) moves the change time back. A program that sets the change time itself through the native API was not tested (E171).
